correctness.rationale: Exact forest inclusion gives (2/n)^r for prescribed matchings. Weighted Prüfer contraction yields the all-finite conditional degree pgf ∏(s_i+t_i)/2 [1+Σ(s_i+t_i−2)/n]^(n−r−2), rigorously implying independent Poisson(1)+fair-Bernoulli marks along any fixed matching. Two-tree independence, overlapping-edge O(n^(−1)) bounds and marked factorial-moment measures prove the spatial PPP of intensity 4dxdy μ⊗μ, and leaf projection gives the nine independent Poisson classes. Exhaustive exact rational checks of 156 finite constraints were reproduced by the packaged standalone checker; these are checks, not substitutes for the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The classical Poisson count of common edges is known and credited. Bender–Canfield (1999) and Bóna–Wagner (2025) give unmarked overlaps and forest-count methods, not the four endpoint degrees of each common edge or their point-process coupling. The exact conditional weighted-Prüfer PGF is not a restatement of their unmarked count and implies nine mutually independent pendant-type limits. Targeted public-record searches found the closest multitreed overlap-cumulant statement but no comparable degree-marked theorem. Full historical priority remains qualified by an inaccessible 1986 source.
residual_risks: Janson (1986) full text was unavailable, so a stronger old theorem cannot be excluded by abstract-only comparison.
A more general, unindexed marked-Poisson theorem for random spanning-tree intersections could imply these results.

value.rationale: The rare overlap point process is a canonical random-tree statistic. Unlike its classical scalar Poisson(2) limit, the result describes an entire marked local-network geometry: correlated endpoint degrees inside each common edge, asymptotically independent profiles across edges, and exact leaf-alignment probabilities 1−exp(−e^(−2)). It gives a complete finite conditional generating function and a coherent infinite-dimensional classification; these are motivated, not arbitrary bounded slices.
